answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 37% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the orchard calculation reruns each epoch, the cedar weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the sparrow settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 176 clones hence holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 3 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
